Prudence means the ability to govern and discipline oneself by using reason and sound judgment, essentially meaning cautious wisdom or practical wisdom. It involves foresight—thinking ahead to consider the long-term consequences of actions, planning carefully, and avoiding unnecessary risks or impulsive behavior.

🧭 Philosophical Context

  • The Cardinal Virtue: Prudence (Latin: prudentia, from providentia meaning "seeing ahead") is traditionally considered one of the four cardinal virtues, directing the others (justice, fortitude, and temperance).
  • "Charioteer of the Virtues": Philosophers like Thomas Aquinas called it the auriga virtutum because it guides the other virtues, discerning the right course of action in specific circumstances.
  • Modern Usage: In modern English, it is often closely associated with cautiousness, discretion, and frugality in managing resources.
